What, then, is the meaning of the pillar of fire? At night, when it is dark, we need the fire. Yet its meaning is the same as that of the cloud. The cloud is fire, and the fire is cloud. When the sun shines, the Lord’s presence is like the appearance of a cloud; when darkness falls, it is like the appearance of fire. It is one and the same thing, only with different forms of appearance.

If that is so, what does the fire signify? It signifies the Word. The cloud is the Spirit, and the fire is the Word. When the sun is shining, you can see very clearly in the Spirit, and you can follow the cloud quite easily. But many times it is just like night, and you are in deep darkness. You may not even be able to trust your own spirit; your spirit may be greatly oppressed. In such a situation, you must rely on the Word. The Word is like a burning fire, shining and giving us light. Psalm 119:105 says, “Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.” When the sky is very clear and everything is bright, the cloud is enough. But when darkness covers the sky and you cannot distinguish which is cloud and which is not, then you must follow the Fire.

ANDAMAN & NICOBAR ISLAND PRESS STUDY TOUR

Today, under the arrangement of the Information & Public Relations Department, 9 members of the Mizoram Journalists Association and 3 I&PR officials left Aizawl for a Press Study Tour to the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

During the Press Study Tour in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, the participants will study various government initiatives and will also meet government officials.

The Press Study Tour will be held from December 9, 2019 to December 15, 2019.

Selected MJA members from different districts of Mizoram are taking part, and they are being led by I&PR Director Pi Lallianpuii, MIS, and Joint Director (Admn) Pu C. Lalnunkima, MIS.

raw_text:
UNION MINISTER SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA HOLDS MEETING IN MAMIT 882/2022-2023 Mamit, 13th June, 2022: Shri Parshottam Rupala, Hon’ble Union Cabinet Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, today held an interaction at the DC Conference Hall, Mamit, with government officials within Mamit town and beneficiaries of various Central Schemes.

At today’s meeting, chaired by Pu Lalnunhlua, Deputy Commissioner, Pu Lalsanglura, Nodal Officer for the Aspirational District Programme, gave a detailed presentation using PowerPoint on the various initiatives being undertaken under the Aspirational District Programme. This was followed by discussion on the progress made and the various future plans and targets.

Shri Parshottam Rupala, Union Minister, explained the reason for his visit to Mamit District and for holding the meeting, saying that he had come to review whether the people of the district were benefiting from the various Central Schemes and whether these were being implemented properly, and to understand and help resolve any difficulties being faced. He also encouraged the district’s concerned officers to study the various government programmes carefully and to work so that the beneficiaries could fully avail themselves of them.

He said that since Mamit District is an Aspirational District, the Centre has made provisions for treatment of serious illnesses with bills up to Rs. 5 lakh, and that out of 5,000 selected persons in Mamit District, 3,000 had already been selected to receive the benefit, while efforts were underway so that the remaining 2,000 could also receive it. He also said that PM-Kisan can be applied for by those who have an Aadhaar Card, land, and a bank account, and urged the concerned departments to ensure that as many farmers as possible in Mamit District receive benefits under the scheme.

The Union Minister said that he would try, as far as possible, to address the problems and needs raised by the government officials and beneficiaries during today’s interaction.

On this occasion, there was also an interaction and question-and-answer session with beneficiaries and concerned officials under various Central Schemes including AYUSHMAN BHARAT - Health & Wellness, Ayushman Bharat - Jan Arogya Yojana, e-Transaction, Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), PM Street Vendor’s Atma Nirbhar Nidhi (PM-SVANidhi

raw_text:
DRAFT ELECTORAL ROLL 2020 PUBLISHED IN LAWNGTLAI

The draft electoral roll for the three Assembly constituencies in Lawngtlai District for 2020 was published yesterday (16.12.2019) by the Lawngtlai District Election Officer, who is also the Deputy Commissioner of Lawngtlai, Pi Shashanka Ala, IAS, in her office chamber. The draft roll was also handed over to representatives of political parties.

According to the published draft electoral roll, in 36-Tuichawng (ST) A/C there are 15,852 male voters and 15,520 female voters, making a total of 31,372; in 37-Lawngtlai West (ST) A/C there are 13,524 male voters and 13,402 female voters, making a total of 26,926; in 38-Lawngtlai East (ST) A/C there are 11,626 male voters and 12,374 female voters, making a total of 24,000. Altogether, in the three Assembly constituencies there are 41,002 male voters and 41,296 female voters, making a total of 82,298 voters.

For this summary revision, time has been given until January 15 of the new year for those who wish to make claims or objections. The final electoral roll is scheduled to be published on February 7, 2020.

raw_text:
Today, as part of the observance of Children’s Week in Mamit, the District Child Protection Unit, Mamit District, organized a Fun Day programme at GSA Playground, Mamit, using the theme “Happy Childhood” as the opening event of Children’s Week.

Pu Shashank Jaiswal, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Mamit, inaugurated the programme and expressed his appreciation to the District Child Protection Unit, Mamit. He said it was commendable and encouraging that they had arranged such an event so that the children of Mamit could spend their time happily. He also said that the safety and happiness of the children of our land rests in everyone’s hands, and at the same time emphasized the importance of cooperation among adults and the community and the need for all to work together. He further stated that if children within Mamit District face any difficulties, the Mamit Police are always there to help them at any time. He encouraged those gathered to make use of such occasions so that children may enjoy memorable, pleasant and happy moments, and to use them as opportunities to further strengthen child protection.

The programme was led by Pi Vanlalruati, PO(IC), DCPU, and Dr. R. Lalrinhlua, DCPO, also spoke about why the Fun Day had been organized for the children of Mamit town and about the importance of giving children leisure time and rest. He said that since children are the future leaders of our country, it is our responsibility to care for them diligently.

At this Fun Day, the DCPU engaged the children with various entertainment activities such as Bouncy, Trampoline, See Saw, Mega Block, Ball Pool, and different games including Spin the Wheel, Ball Kick, Dart Game, Cup Game, Ball Score, Photo Booth, Talent Hunt, and Bow and Arrow. Child Care Institutions also set up different stalls and made these recreational activities available for children to enjoy free of charge.

The children greatly valued the event, and a large number of children from Mamit town attended.

Principal Secretary, Higher & Technical Education Department leh Chairman State Selection Board Committee ni bawk chuan thuchhuah siamin State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022 atana online a dilna thehluh hun tawp ni (last date of submission) chu Zirtawpni, June ni 3, 2022 zan 11:50 thlenga pawhsei a ni tiin he exam bei tum zirlaite a hriattir a. reference: Government of Mizoram postpone Smartee Exam 47/2022-2023 Aizawl, the 11th May 2022; As shown below, the Government of Mizoram postponed the date of examination for State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022. The last date & time of submission of online application form for State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022 notified vide this Office Order No.A.45011/2/2021-JDT(HTE) dated Aizawl, the 11th April, 2022 is hereby extended up to the 3rd June, 2022 (Friday) 11:59 pm. Further, the date of examination of SMATEE 2022 is also hereby postponed on the 17th June,2022 (Friday) between 11:00 am - 2:00 pm.
hypothesis: Government postpones SMATEE Exam 471/2022-2023 Aizawl, 11th May 2022: As stated below, the Government of Mizoram has postponed the scheduled date for holding the State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022. The Principal Secretary, Higher & Technical Education Department, who is also the Chairman of the State Selection Board Committee, stated in a press release that the last date for submitting online applications for the State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022 has been extended till 11:50 p.m. on Friday, 3rd June 2022, and informed students intending to appear for the exam accordingly. He also informed that the SMATEE 2022 exam has been rescheduled to Friday, 17th June 2022.

The Principal Secretary, Higher & Technical Education Department, who is also the Chairman of the State Selection Board Committee, stated in a press release that the last date for submitting online applications for the State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022 has been extended till 11:50 p.m. on Friday, 3rd June 2022, and informed students intending to appear for the exam accordingly. He also informed that the SMATEE 2022 exam has been rescheduled to Friday, 17th June 2022.

hypothesis: Life was created to be capable of being corrupted and defiled. For example, suppose we instruct our children at home not to play with the blackboard chalk. After I leave the house, out of sheer curiosity they play with the chalk; then when I return, I discover that they have done wrong. Their wrongdoing is only a violation of household rules, and nothing has entered into them. However, suppose on another occasion I leave at home a bottle containing very dangerous medicine and tell the children, “Do not ever drink this.” After I leave the house, they discover that the bottle is very tempting to open—and in the end they drink the very dangerous poisonous medicine. Here, they have not merely broken the family rule and disobeyed my command; worse than that, something dangerous has entered into them. In exactly this way, when Adam ate from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, this is what happened. He not only disobeyed what God had forbidden, but Satan’s life also entered into him. At that very point, man’s inward being became thoroughly corrupted; besides the good, upright, and proper human life he originally had, he also came to possess the corrupted and sinful life of Satan.

source: COMMERCE & INDUSTRIES MINISTER-IN LUNGLEIAH AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING HAWNG No.4122/2021-2022 Aizawl, the 26 th February 2022 : Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana chuan vawiin khan Electric Veng, Lungleiah NABARD sum cheng nuai 1082.93 senga ruahman Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building a hawng. Hawnna inkhawm Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary, Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi kaihhruaiah Dr R Lalthangliana chuan Lunglei khawpui chhunga hmasawnna ruhrel liantham, khawtlang tana chhenfakawm tak leh eizawnna kawnga tangkai taka hman theih tur Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building zawhfel a ni chu lawmawm tiin a buaipuitu Commerce & Industries thawktute, building sa tu te leh Electric Veng Lunglei khawtlang te chungah lawmthu a sawi a. C&I Department hnuaiah hmalakna hrang hrang kalpui mek zel anih thu sawiin Lunglei Supermarket sakna tur cheng nuai 1400 NEC atanga sanction hmuh anih thu sawiin Bangladesh ram nena kan insumdawn tawnna atana ruahman Integrated Check Post (ICP), Kawrpuichhuah, Tlabung ti hlawhtling turin Department chuan theihtawp a chhuah mek zel thu a sawi a ni. A Department chan dangte hnuaia hmalaknte pawh sawilangin Minister chuan MZU Southern Campus atan DPR cheng vaibelchhe 400 sawrkar laipuiah thehluh tawh niin chak taka bawhzui mek a ni a, MZU Southern Campus tana hman lailawk tur Engineering College building chei that hna pawh thawh mek a ni, a ti a. Civil Hospital Lungleia Trauma Centre sak pawh zawh fel thuai beisei anih thu sawiin Multipurpose Laboratory Building, NEC sum cheng nuai 300 a ruahman mek pawh nakum kum tir lama zawhfel beisei anih thu a sawi. Lunglei Municipal Council (LMC) chungchang pawh sawiin Minister chuan Municipal body chak tak enkawlna hnuaiah Lunglei khawpui chuan kawng hrang hrangin hmasawnna a nei dawn a ni, a ti. He huna khualzahawm Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng chuan Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building hawn theiha peih fel a ni ta chu Pathian malsawmna ropui tak a ni tiin he hmasawnna ruhrel neih theihna tura sulsutute thawhrimna leh thahnemngaihna rah a ni, a ti a. He building ti hlawhtling tura bultan tu Pu Joseph Lalhimpuia chungah leh a hmun phal taka petu Electric Veng YMA te chungah lawmthu a sawi a ni. He building sak enkawltu AIE Constructions, Tuikhuahtlang, Aizawl atangin Technical Report ngaihtlak a ni a. Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure hi NABARD, RIDF XXIII hnuaia project niin total project cost hi Rs. 1082.93 lakhs ani a. Hna hi 05/10/2018 ah thawh tan a ni. A building plinth area hi 574.875 Square metres niin building hi floor nga (5) a sak a ni a. First floor hi Agriculture leh marketing lama training leh awareness centre atan ruahman niin mihring 300 vel leng tura hisap a ni. Ground floor ah hian guest room, conference/meeting room te awmin Basement I ah hian mi 78 lenna market area bakah market office ruamhan niin Basement II ah mi 85 lenna market area niin Basement III hi motor 25 lenna parking area-a ruahman a ni. reference: AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING INAUGURATED AT LUNGLEI No.523/2021-2022 Aizawl, the 28th February 2022 : Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana on Saturday (26th February, 2022) inaugurated Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building at Electric Veng, Lunglei. The Rs. 1082.93 lakhs project is implemented under the NABARD, RIDF XXIII. Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng was the guest of honour at the inauguration. At the inaugural function chaired by Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary, Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi, Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana commended C&I Department staff, Electric veng YMA, VCs for their contribution towards successful completion of the project. As per Technical Report presented by AIE Constructions, Tuikhuahtlang, Aizawl, the 5 floors Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building has a plinth area of 574.875 Square metres. The first floor is intended to be used as a training and awareness centre for agriculture marketing with an estimated capacity of 300 people, with guest rooms, conference/meeting rooms at the Ground floor. Basement I and Basement II contain the market areas and market offices, with a parking area at the basement.

raw_text:
COMMERCE & INDUSTRIES MINISTER OPENS AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING IN LUNGLEI

No.4122/2021-2022  
Aizawl, the 26th February 2022:

Today, Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr. R. Lalthangliana inaugurated the Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building at Electric Veng, Lunglei, constructed at a cost of Rs. 1082.93 lakhs under NABARD funding.

At the inauguration function, chaired by Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi, Dr. R. Lalthangliana expressed happiness over the completion of the Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building, which he described as a major development asset within Lunglei town, something commendable for the local community, and one that can be usefully utilized for livelihood purposes. He thanked the Commerce & Industries staff who worked on it, those who constructed the building, and the residents of Electric Veng, Lunglei.

He said that various initiatives are continuously being undertaken under the C&I Department. He mentioned that Rs. 1400 lakhs has been sanctioned by NEC for the construction of the Lunglei Supermarket, and that the Department is making every effort to successfully implement the proposed Integrated Check Post (ICP) at Kawrpuichhuah, Tlabung, intended for trade with Bangladesh.

Referring also to initiatives under other departments, the Minister said that a DPR worth Rs. 400 crore for MZU Southern Campus has already been submitted to the central government and is being actively pursued. Renovation work on the Engineering College building, to be used temporarily for MZU Southern Campus, is also underway, he said.

He further stated that the Trauma Centre at Civil Hospital, Lunglei is expected to be completed soon, and that the Multipurpose Laboratory Building, being planned under NEC funding of Rs. 300 lakhs, is also expected to be completed in the early part of next year.

Speaking about the Lunglei Municipal Council (LMC), the Minister said that under the strong administration of the municipal body, Lunglei town will see progress in various ways.

On this occasion, the chief guest, Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng, said that the completion and opening of the Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building was a great blessing from God, and that this development project was the fruit of the hard work and dedication

raw_text:
RAJYA SABHA MP PU K. VANLALVENA SUBMITS THE ISSUE OF THE SUFFERING OF THE PEOPLE OF MYANMAR TO THE VICE PRESIDENT OF INDIA

No. 7795/2020-2021  
Aizawl, 15th March, 2021:

Rajya Sabha MP Pu K. Vanlalvena, who is currently in Delhi for the Parliament Budget Session, today called on the Vice President of India and also Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Pu M. Venkaiah Naidu, at his residence and discussed with him the severe suffering being faced by those striving to restore democracy in Myanmar, along with other important needs of Mizoram. Pu Vena was accompanied by MNF Adviser Pu Rosangzuala.

He informed the Vice President that because of the crisis in Myanmar, many people had already been killed and injured at the hands of the military, many had been imprisoned, that the exact number of those killed and injured due to the unrest could not yet be known, and that the numbers appeared likely to continue increasing. He also told him that some members of the Myanmar military and police, unwilling to act against the people of Myanmar, had surrendered their arms and, along with some other civilians, had fled to Mizoram seeking refuge.

They also conveyed that it was necessary to consider assistance for these refugees fleeing from Myanmar, and appealed to the Vice President of India to take appropriate steps to bring an end to the suffering of the people of Myanmar. They further stated that they felt it was necessary to review the Central Government’s policy toward Myanmar.

Pu Vena and Pu Rosangzuala also requested the Vice President to help ensure that a Mizo person be appointed to the Union Public Service Commission, since not even one person from Mizoram has ever served as a member of the UPSC since India became independent. They also informed the Vice President that even after 35 years of attaining full statehood, Mizoram still remains under the AGMUT cadre in the All India Civil Services, which they said was no longer appropriate, and that the time had come to create a separate Mizoram cadre.

They also requested Vice President Pu M. Venkaiah Naidu to consider making it possible for applicants for jobs under the Staff Selection Commission to take their examinations in Aizawl, so that they would no longer have to go all the way to Guwahati for the exams.

reference: VDVK LEVEL ADVOCACY PROGRAMME ON PMVDY HELD AT KAWRTHAH No.342/2021-2022 Aizawl 8th October, 2021 : Van Dhan Vikas Kendra (VDVK) Level Advocacy Programme under Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana (PMVDY) was held at SSA Block Resource Centre at Kawrthah Mamit District under the leadership of Pu Lalthangfala, District Cooperative Officer Mamit District. Under Kawrthah VDVK Centre targetted beneficiaries of 300 tribal women from Kawrthah cluster will be trained in tailoring. Awareness programme regarding VDVK under PMVDY was held for the trainees under the initiative of Mamit District Cooperative Office. Attachment Loading attachment...
hypothesis: PMVDY under VDVK Level Advocacy Programme held at Kawrthah. No.2537/2021-2022 Aizawl, 8th October, 2021: Today at Kawrthah village, under the Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana (PMVDY), a VDVK Level Advocacy Programme and Entrepreneurship and Skill Development Programme training was held. Pu Lalthangfala, District Cooperative Officer, Mamit, attended as chief guest and inaugurated the programme. The chief guest said that a weaving training centre for Mizo women would be opened at the Kawrthah village VDVK Centre and that weaving looms would be distributed under the Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana (PMVDY). He urged the weaving trainees to be diligent and to take the training seriously as a means of livelihood. Today, this awareness programme was conducted for 300 women interested in weaving, in batches of 40 each, while observing Covid Appropriate Behaviour.

raw_text:
LUNGLEI DISTRICT - COVID-19 NO TOLERANCE FORTNIGHT No.6374/2020-2021

As the Covid-19 pandemic is spreading rapidly and there is a possibility of continued transmission, and in order that the public may be able to live in compliance with the restrictions imposed because of Covid-19, the Mizoram Government has planned the Covid-19 “No Tolerance Fortnight” from 26 October to 9 November 2020, and this is being strictly implemented in Lunglei District. At the same time, the Jan Andolan Campaign to educate people on safety measures relating to Covid-19 is also continuing.

Yesterday, under the leadership of Lunglei DC & DLTF Chairman Pu V. Lalsangliana, a meeting was held in his office chamber where the detailed manner of implementing the Covid-19 No Tolerance Fortnight in Lunglei District was discussed. During the No Tolerance Fortnight, 30 employees each from every government department have been assigned for Covid-19 Executive Duty, divided into 24 teams, and their duties have been arranged. Each team will have a Team Leader, and they will widely inform the public about guidelines for protection against Covid-19, and those who do not follow the guidelines will be fined without leniency.

These Covid-19 Executive Duty personnel will strictly enforce the provisions laid down for the public under The Mizoram (Containment and Prevention of Spread of Covid-19) Act, 2020 and the government orders issued thereunder, and against those found violating the law, penalty slips will be issued and proper challans prepared, and they will be made to pay the prescribed amount of fine. Lunglei District has also been divided into eight zones, and an Executive Magistrate/Incident Commander has been appointed for each zone.

From today, in coordination with the VLTFs of every locality, Covid-19 Executive Duty has begun throughout Lunglei District. During the Covid-19 No Tolerance Fortnight, talk shows to re-inform the public of various important matters relating to Covid-19 will be arranged through Local Cable. Banners on protection against Covid-19 have also been put up at important places in Lunglei town. The VLTFs have also been requested to make loudspeaker announcements three times daily in different localities/villages regarding Covid-19 prevention and guidelines.
